clue.text: I'm frustrated because dog hides when ready to return

parts.note: for can mean because, as in 'for he was tired'

indicators.note: the dog hides the next piece, so it is put inside the dog's name

parts.note: a peke is a Pekingese, a small Chinese dog breed

indicators.note: to return means the words for when and ready are read backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as the clock struck'
set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go' or 'all set'

explanation.surface: Someone snaps in exasperation because the dog is hiding just when they are ready to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To return' turns 'when ready' into TESSA, which the Chinese lapdog 'hides'; the apostrophe in the phrase is not entered in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an everyday cry of exasperation, which is what a speaker means by saying they are frustrated.

clue.text: Wrinkling and hair falling out

parts.note: fur is the hair of an animal
a row is a quarrel, so rowing (rhyming with cowing) means falling out

explanation.surface: A complaint that the forehead creases while the hair drops out: signs of ageing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling out' reads as hair loss but means quarrelling, ROWING in the sense of having a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Furrowing the brow is creasing it into lines, a synonym for wrinkling.

clue.text: Sage butter is hideous to sample

indicators.note: to sample is to take a small part, so the answer is a run of letters taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A cook's verdict that sage butter tastes hideous when you try it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sage' looks like the herb flavouring the butter, but it is the definition: a wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu holy man or seer, a wise person, which is a sage.

clue.text: Learner in school is John, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the learner's letter inside the school's name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A pupil at a school is named as John, as if on a register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' is not a schoolboy: Elton John is the singer, so the answer is a first name that goes with John.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John is the pop star, so Elton is an example of a name paired with John.

clue.text: Environmentally bad bar vainly struggling for registration

indicators.note: bad signals the letters of the first word are scrambled
bar means except, so the letters of the following word are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: An environmentally harmful bar struggles in vain to sign people up.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive anagram: 'bad' scrambles ENVIRONMENTALLY, 'bar' removes the letters of VAINLY (themselves 'struggling', in any order), leaving a scramble of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of signing up for a course or list, which is registration.

clue.text: Exhibit hospital in broadcast item

indicators.note: in places the hospital's letter inside the word for broadcast

parts.note: to sow seed is to scatter it, the original sense of broadcast
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a piece is an item, as in a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A display piece about a hospital appears in a broadcast programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio or TV but here means scattering seed: SOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding item put on display, an exhibit.

clue.text: Capsized glossy boats

indicators.note: a capsized vessel is turned over, so in a down clue the word is read upside down, backwards

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy, as of hair or fur

explanation.surface: Smart shiny boats have overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: Keel is a poetic word for a whole ship, by naming the part for the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Keel, by synecdoche, means a ship in poetry, so keels are boats.

clue.text: The poorest orders in hierarchy are given here

definitions.meaning: the underclass is the lowest, poorest stratum of society

definitions.text: orders in hierarchy are given here
definitions.meaning: in biological taxonomy, orders rank just below classes

explanation.surface: A grim remark that the poorest people simply receive orders from those above them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' and 'hierarchy' suggest social command, but they are ranks in taxonomy: kingdom, phylum, class, order. Split the answer (5,7) to read it.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclasses are the most deprived groups in society, the poorest of all.

clue.text: Bugs enter chest in opposing directions

indicators.note: enter puts the chest between the two compass letters

parts.note: north and south, N and S, are opposite compass points
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Insects get into a chest, crawling every which way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' looks like insects but is a verb: annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark is British slang for to irritate, so narks means annoys, which bugs does too.

clue.text: Money from selling small pies

parts.note: turnover is the total money a business takes from sales
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A baker's takings from a sale of little pies.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first part reads as the definition, but it gives TURNOVER; 'pies' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a pastry folded over a filling, a kind of small pie.

clue.text: Cross men seek to confound cover-ups

indicators.note: to confound is to throw into confusion, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Angry men set out to confuse those hiding the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A smokescreen is something meant to disguise real intentions, so smokescreens are cover-ups.

clue.text: Moving book recalled Scottish island lake

indicators.note: recalled, called back, means this word is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a book, usually a big one
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A touching book remembers a lake on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving stirs the feelings, which is what emotional means.

clue.text: Undesirable duck sauce

parts.note: a pest is an undesirable person or creature
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: A cook frowns on the sauce served with duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck sauce' looks like a dish, but duck is nought, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and cheese.

clue.text: Naive daughter tucked into spicy dish, not half keen

indicators.note: tucked into puts the daughter's letter inside the dish

parts.note: chilli is short for chilli con carne, a spicy dish
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A trusting girl eats a spicy dish with only moderate enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' reads as eating, but it puts the daughter inside the dish; 'not half' leaves only the first two letters of 'keen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Childlike means having a child's innocence and simplicity, which is being naive.

clue.text: Centre in Bordeaux housing big silo to recycle refuse

indicators.note: housing means the centre letters hold the next piece inside them
the centre of an eight-letter word is its middle two letters
to recycle is to reprocess, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A French city's central depot holds a big silo for recycling rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like rubbish but is a verb: to fail to oblige someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To disoblige is to act against someone's wishes, declining to help: to refuse them.

clue.text: I'm getting old, short and fairly regularly ignored — it's not real!

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: aging, also spelt ageing, means getting old

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone protests that being old and short and routinely overlooked can't really be happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly regularly ignored' drops F, I, L of 'fairly', leaving ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Imaginary describes what exists only in the mind, so of it one says it's not real.

clue.text: Destroy quiet, primarily rural parts

indicators.note: parts means the word for quiet is split apart by the letter going inside it

parts.note: ease is peace and quiet, as in 'at ease'

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An order to wreck quiet, mostly country districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' reads as a noun, regions, but it is a verb: the R divides EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out completely, a synonym for destroy.

clue.text: Deed reportedly you sign for assessors

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: you sounds the same as the letter U
Aries the ram is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An instruction that a legal deed requires your signature before the assessors see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a verb, as in signing a deed, but it is a star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Actuaries assess insurance risks and calculate premiums, so they are professional assessors.

clue.text: Occasionally take against guard

indicators.note: occasionally means taking letters now and then, here every other one

explanation.surface: Advice to sometimes act defensively against a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Aegis is protection or sponsorship, from the shield of Zeus, so it is a guard.

clue.text: Anagram in that clue omitting L? True

indicators.note: the word Anagram itself orders a shuffle of the letters

parts.note: taken as written as the pool of letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A solver asks whether the anagram in that clue really works without the L.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Omitting L' removes the L from IN THAT CLUE before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means genuine and real, which is what true means here.

clue.text: Cleanser customer emptied in vessel

indicators.note: in places the outer letters inside the vessel

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a vessel

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside of the word, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shop's cleaning product, a customer's emptied bottle in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a pot or bottle, but it is a submarine: SUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrub is a cleansing preparation rubbed on the skin, a cleanser.

clue.text: Large beast in grass; be aware, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the words are heard, so the spelling differs

parts.note: rye is a cereal grass and to know is to be aware, so the words said are rye know

explanation.surface: A warning that a big animal lurks in the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinoceros is a huge horned animal, a large beast.

clue.text: Worry about one on popular junction

indicators.note: on means placed after, as in an across clue one piece comes on another

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: about means the word for worry is turned round

parts.note: to fret is to worry
an ace is a playing card with a value of one

explanation.surface: Concern about a single item placed on something popular, at a meeting point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns the worry word round to TERF; in an across clue, 'A on B' means A follows B.
explanation.definitionFit: An interface is the point where two systems meet and connect, so it is a junction.

clue.text: Sense leader in country should be demoted

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, which is the one that moves
demoted means moved lower, so in a down entry the first letter drops further down

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A view that the nation's leader deserves a demotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of STATE moves down two places to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, so it is an example of a sense.

clue.text: One speeding about, vehicle coming north

indicators.note: coming north means read upwards, and in a down entry that turns both words backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning, as in business letters
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone driving fast nearby as a vehicle heads north.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is someone or something that goes fast in a race, one speeding.

clue.text: Covered in wounds, not totally afraid around weapons

indicators.note: covered in means the shortened word is wrapped inside the word for wounds

parts.note: scars are the marks of wounds, here standing for wounds

indicators.note: around means this word is turned about, read backwards
not totally means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: timid means afraid or nervous

explanation.surface: A fighter covered in wounds, not entirely fearless, near his weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not totally' drops the last letter of the word for afraid and 'around' turns the rest to IMIT; the wounds are named by the marks they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Scimitars are curved oriental swords, so they are examples of weapons.

clue.text: Marker that's raised Scots kid's initially downgraded mark

indicators.note: the first letter is a grade, and downgrading it by one mark turns B into the next grade down

parts.note: bairn is the Scots word for a child; the 's is part of the surface

explanation.surface: A child's school grade has been lowered, marked down for raising a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Grades run A, B, C: downgrading the initial B by one mark gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a heap of stones piled up as a landmark or memorial, a raised marker.

clue.text: Single people new in hostelry getting drunk with ale

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the scrambled letters
getting drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Singles, a newcomer among them, get drunk on ale in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A hostelry is an inn or pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely hearts are people seeking a partner, as in newspaper ads, so they are single people.
